thread:
Anya (Marketing): Quick sync — need a tight benchmark narrative for launch. Goal: 1 short social post, 3 slides for the webinar, + one micro-chart for docs. Core message should be: small latency improvements => outsized cost savings at scale. Who can draft framing + chart asks?

Ravi (Growth): I can take the copy for the social post and the headline line for slide 1. Proposed headline: "Faster tokens, lower bills: how latency tuning shrinks inference cost". Need numbers to make it punchy.

Jon (Product): For slides I suggest 3 frames:
- Slide A: latency curve (x = p95 latency, y = cost per 1M tokens) — line showing cost rises as latency increases due to wasted tail + smaller batches.
- Slide B: two bars: cold vs cached/hot (same model) showing tokens consumed & $/100k requests.
- Slide C: routing playbook — cost vs SLA table (hosted, dedicated, private).

Leah (Design): Chart specs: keep it tiny (900x540 px), 2 color palette (brand blue + charcoal). Axis labels: "p95 latency (ms)" and "$/1M tokens". Add a subtle dashed SLO line at 200ms. I'll mock the mini-chart.

Sam (Data): I can run the experiment to produce real points. Quick plan: take 3 models 7B/13B/70B, run synthetic workload with token distribution from our median customer. Measure cost per 100k requests at p50/p95/p99 with and without KV prefix caching. ETA: raw CSV by EOD Thursday.

Anya (Marketing): Perfect. For the social post we want a one-liner + subline. Ravi, can you draft 1-liner + CTA? Keep it product-forward, not too technical.

Ravi (Growth): Draft: "Cut inference bills by up to 3x — optimize latency, not just model size. See our benchmark + webinar." Subline: "Live demo + micro-charts: how caching, batching, and routing change the economics of LLMs. Register: https://redwood.example/webinar" 

Jon (Product): One note for the slides: call out assumptions in small footnote — token length distribution, request concurrency, and whether embeddings included. Also show the fallback policy that keeps user-facing latency while routing cheap requests to optimized variants.

Leah (Design): I'll produce 2 versions: one for the webinar deck (wide) and one as an embed for the blog (square). Filenames: latencycurve_v1.png, latencycurve_embed_v1.png. Want the raw CSV to annotate points.

Sam (Data): CSV schema: model, run_id, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_request, cost_per_1M_tokens_usd, cached_boolean. Example row:
```
13B, run-2026-03-24-01, 48, 210, 480, 92, 12.34, true
```
I'll add columns for batching factor and average KV hit rate.

Anya (Marketing): Routing / inbound asks: we want two lead buckets:
- "Econ Curious": people who download the one-pager and get the 1-pager flow via automated email.
- "Sales Warm": customers who request dedicated benchmarks or private deploy — route to AE queue with "benchmark-request" tag.
Make the CTA language match the social post.

Ravi (Growth): For the landing page we should auto-tag utm_source=bench_launch and add a hidden attribute to flag high-qps demos (qps > 50) so SDRs can prioritize. Also add a short form question: "Are you evaluating performance at scale? (Yes / No)" to route.

Jon (Product): Add a tiny script snippet on the docs page for people to reproduce the test locally. Something like:
```
# run synthetic workload
python run_bench.py --model redwood-13b --concurrency 8 --tokens 1024 --cache true
```
Keep it simple so engineers can sanity-check our numbers.

Leah (Design): UX nit: include a caption under the chart with the single-most-actionable stat, e.g. "Latency tuning + caching reduced $/1M tokens by 45% in our median workload". Big number = shareable.

Sam (Data): I'll compute the 95% CI for cost savings and include a small table: mean savings, lower/upper bounds. Will deliver both CSV and a simple chart-ready JSON.

Anya (Marketing): Owners & deadlines:
- Benchmark CSV + initial numbers: Sam — Thu EOD (1762580000)
- Slide + micro-chart mock: Leah — Fri AM
- Social + landing copy + form: Ravi — Fri EOD
- Product notes + code snippet: Jon — Fri EOD
- Final review + publish plan: Anya — next Tue AM

Ravi (Growth): I'll also prep a 30s teaser video (screen capture of the three slides + headline) for LinkedIn and X. Need the mock by Fri noon to hit next-week cadence. :rocket:

Jon (Product): Quick question — should we include a 4th mini-variant comparing quantized vs non-quantized runs? That could be a high-impact callout.

Sam (Data): Yes, add quantization flag. I'll add two extra rows per run with quantized=true/false. It won't change the timeline.

Anya (Marketing): Great. If nobody objects, we'll go with this plan. Thanks all — will circle back with a short publish checklist once drafts come in. :thumbsup:
